security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown code fences or inline formatting, so they are false positives. The listed URLs are support resources, not automatic network behavior. The remaining risk is that setup examples use unpinned npm and npx package execution for an external MCP service.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package execution in setup examples
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact flow-nexus and claude-flow versions, and document package verification before users run npm or npx commands.
Document what workflow data is sent to Flow Nexus, required authentication scopes, and cleanup expectations.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote CLI Setup Commands
semantic_findings.description: The setup and integration examples tell users to run npm or npx packages using @latest or @alpha and add an MCP server. Those commands execute third-party package code that can change over time unless versions are pinned and verified.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced lines explicitly show npx, npm install, and MCP setup commands with @alpha or @latest version selectors. This is a real supply-chain and reproducibility risk, although it appears to be setup documentation rather than hidden execution.

content.value_statement: Coordinating many AI agents across cloud workflows is hard to plan and monitor. This skill gives patterns for Flow Nexus swarms, queues, templates, and workflow automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize swarms with hierarchical, mesh, ring, or star topologies.
Shows MCP calls for spawning agents, orchestrating tasks, scaling swarms, and destroying swarms.
Documents workflow creation, execution, status checks, audit trails, and queue monitoring.
Provides patterns for full-stack development, research, CI/CD, and data processing pipelines.
Lists Flow Nexus templates and setup commands for Claude Code MCP integration.
limitations: Requires the Flow Nexus MCP server and an active Flow Nexus account.
Examples depend on the external Flow Nexus cloud service being available.
The skill provides documentation patterns, not a local workflow engine.
Users must validate workflow actions and permissions before production use.

use_cases.title: Plan Multi-Agent Development
use_cases.description: Define agent roles, swarm topology, workflow dependencies, and monitoring steps for a software project.

use_cases.title: Automate Deployment Workflows
use_cases.description: Model testing, building, scanning, staging, production deployment, and rollback as a Flow Nexus workflow.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Research Pipelines
use_cases.description: Split research, analysis, synthesis, and reporting across multiple specialized cloud agents.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Swarm Topology
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a Flow Nexus topology for [project]. Recommend agent types, a maximum agent count, and the first task to orchestrate.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workflow Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Flow Nexus workflow for [process]. Include steps, dependencies, triggers, retry policy, monitoring, and cleanup requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an existing Flow Nexus template with project-specific changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a Flow Nexus template for [goal]. Explain needed overrides, agent roles, queue settings, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multiple Swarms
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a large program.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan multiple Flow Nexus swarms for [large initiative]. Define phase boundaries, handoffs, shared audit trails, scaling triggers, and shutdown steps.

output_examples.input: I need a CI/CD workflow for a web service with security checks.
output: Recommended topology: hierarchical, with a coordinator, test runner, builder, security agent, and deployer.
Workflow stages: lint, unit tests, integration tests, build, security scan, staging deploy, smoke test, production deploy.
Monitoring focus: audit trail, queue status, retry count, and rollback readiness.

output_examples.input: I want to run a market research task with several AI agents.
output: Recommended topology: mesh, because research agents can compare findings in parallel.
Suggested agents: primary researcher, secondary researcher, data analyst, and insights analyst.
Execution mode: parallel task orchestration with a final synthesis step.

output_examples.input: I need to scale a running swarm that is overloaded.
output: Check swarm status and current workload before changing capacity.
Increase the target agent count only when queue depth or workload justifies it.
Destroy unused swarms after completion to limit cost and operational exposure.

best_practices: Choose topology from workflow shape, not agent count alone.
Use asynchronous execution for long-running workflows and monitor queue status.
Destroy swarms after work completes to reduce cost and exposure.
anti_patterns: Do not run production workflows without reviewing agent permissions and actions.
Do not use latest package tags when reproducible installations are required.
Do not create large swarms before defining clear task boundaries.

faq.question: Does this skill run Flow Nexus by itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents how to use the Flow Nexus MCP server and related commands.

faq.question: Is a Flow Nexus account required?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that an active Flow Nexus account is required.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude Code setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Claude Code MCP setup command for Flow Nexus.

faq.question: What swarm topologies are covered?
faq.answer: It covers hierarchical, mesh, ring, and star topologies.

faq.question: Does it support workflow monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers workflow status, queue status, audit trails, and execution streams.

faq.question: What should users review before production use?
faq.answer: Review package versions, cloud data handling, workflow actions, permissions, and cleanup steps.
